# PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES] Contents of this Part

## Scope of this Part

## 21.1

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (1) This Part –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (a) contains special provisions which apply in proceedings involving children and protected parties;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (b) sets out how a person becomes a litigation friend; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (c) does not apply to— (i) proceedings under Part 75; (ii) enforcement of specified debts by taking control of goods; or (iii) applications in relation to enforcement of specified debts by taking control of goods, where one of the parties to the proceedings is a child. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (2) In this Part –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (a) ‘the 2005 Act’ means the Mental Capacity Act 2005;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (b) ‘child’ means a person under 18;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (c) ‘lacks capacity’ means lacks capacity within the meaning of the 2005 Act;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (d) ‘protected party’ means a party, or an intended party, who lacks capacity to conduct the proceedings;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (e) ‘protected beneficiary’ means a protected party who lacks capacity to manage and control any money recovered by them or on their behalf or for their benefit in the proceedings. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (f) ‘specified debts’ has the same meaning as in rule 75.1(2)(e); and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (g) ‘taking control of goods’ means using the procedure to take control of goods contained in Schedule 12 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007 1 . [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (Rules 6.13 and 6.25 contain provisions about the service of documents on children and protected parties.)

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.1] (Rule 46.4 deals with costs where money is payable by or to a child or protected party.)

## Requirement for a litigation friend in proceedings by or against children and protected parties

## 21.2

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (1) A protected party must have a litigation friend to conduct proceedings on their behalf. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (2) Unless the court makes an order under paragraph (3), a litigation friend must conduct proceedings on a child’s behalf. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (3) The court may make an order permitting a child to conduct proceedings without a litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (4) An application for an order under paragraph (3) –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (a) may be made by the child;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (b) if the child already has a litigation friend, must be made on notice to the litigation friend; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (c) if the child has no litigation friend, may be made without notice. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (5) Where –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (a) the court has made an order under paragraph (3); and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (b) it later appears to the court desirable for a litigation friend to conduct the proceedings on the child’s behalf, the court may appoint a person to be the child’s litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (6) Where one of the parties is a child or protected party, that party shall be referred to in the title to the proceedings as “[name] (a [child] [protected party]) by [name] as litigation friend”. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.2] (7) Where one of the parties is a child conducting the proceedings on their own behalf, the child shall be referred to in the title as “[name] (a child)”. ## Stage of proceedings at which a litigation friend becomes necessary

## 21.3

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (1) This rule does not apply where the court has made an order under rule 21.2(3). [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (2) A person may not, without the  court’s permission –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (a) make an application against a child or protected party before proceedings have started; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (b) take any step in proceedings except –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (i) issuing and serving a claim form; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (ii) applying for the appointment of a litigation friend under rule 21.6,

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] until the child or protected party has a litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (3) If during proceedings a party lacks capacity to continue to conduct proceedings, no party may take any further step in the proceedings without the court’s permission until the protected party has a litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.3] (4) Any step taken before a child or protected party has a litigation friend has no effect unless the court orders otherwise. ## Who may be a litigation friend without a court order

## 21.4

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (1) This rule does not apply if the court has appointed a person to be a litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (2) A deputy appointed by the Court of Protection under the 2005 Act with power to conduct proceedings on the protected party’s behalf is entitled to be the protected party’s litigation friend in any proceedings to which the deputy’s power extends. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (3) If nobody has been appointed by the court or, in the case of a protected party, appointed as a deputy as set out in paragraph (2), a person may act as a litigation friend if they –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (a) can fairly and competently conduct proceedings on behalf of the child or protected party;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (b) have no interest adverse to that of the child or protected party; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.4] (c) where the child or protected party is a claimant, undertake to pay any costs that the claimant is ordered to pay, subject to any right to be repaid from the assets of the child or protected party. ## How a person becomes a litigation friend without a court order

## 21.5

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (1) If the court has not appointed a litigation friend, a person who wishes to act as a litigation friend must follow the procedure set out in this rule. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (2) A deputy appointed by the Court of Protection under the 2005 Act with power to conduct proceedings on the protected party’s behalf must file an official copy (GL) of the order of the Court of Protection which confers their power to act either –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (a) where the protected party is to be a claimant, when the claim is made; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (b) where the protected party is to be a defendant, at the time when the deputy first takes a step in the proceedings on the defendant’s behalf. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (3) Any other person must file a certificate of suitability stating that they satisfy the conditions specified in rule 21.4(3) either –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (a) where the person is to act as a litigation friend for a claimant, at the time when the claim is made; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (b) where the person is to act as a litigation friend for a defendant, at the time when they first take a step in the proceedings on the defendant’s behalf. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (4) The certificate of suitability must be verified by a statement of truth and must state in accordance with the prescribed form that the person—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (a )agrees to act;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (b) knows or believes the person concerned is a child or lacks capacity to conduct the proceedings (stating in the latter case the grounds for that knowledge or belief); and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (c) meets the requirements of rule 21.4(3)

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (5) The litigation friend must –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (a) serve the certificate of suitability on every person on whom, in accordance with rule 6.13 (service on a parent, guardian etc.), the claim form should be served; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (b) file a certificate of service when filing the certificate of suitability. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (6) Where the grounds for believing that a protected party lacks capacity to conduct the litigation are based on expert opinion, a copy of such opinion must be served, either with the certificate of suitability or separately. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.5] (Rules 6.17 and 6.29 set out the details to be contained in a certificate of service.)

## How a person becomes a litigation friend by court order

## 21.6

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (1) The court may make an order appointing a litigation friend. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (2) An application for an order appointing a litigation friend may be made under Part 23 by –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (a) a person who wishes to be the litigation friend; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (b) a party. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (3) Where –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (a) a person makes a claim against a child or protected party;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (b) the child or protected party has no litigation friend;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (c) the court has not made an order under rule 21.2(3) (order that a child can conduct proceedings without a litigation friend); and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (d) either –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (i) someone who is not entitled to be a litigation friend files a defence; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (ii) the claimant wishes to take some step in the proceedings,

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] the claimant must apply to the court for an order appointing a litigation friend for the child or protected party. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (4) An application for an order appointing a litigation friend must be supported by evidence of all the matters set out in rule 21.4(3). [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (5) The court may not appoint a litigation friend under this rule unless it is satisfied of those matters. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.6] (6) Where the proposed litigation friend is the Official Solicitor, the court’s order must make provision for payment of any charges, expenses or disbursements. ## Court’s power to change a litigation friend and to prevent person acting as a litigation friend

## 21.7

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (1) The court may –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (a) direct that a person may not act as a litigation friend;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (b) terminate a litigation friend’s appointment; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (c) appoint a new litigation friend instead of an existing one. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (2) An application for an order under paragraph (1) must be supported by evidence. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.7] (3) The court may not appoint a litigation friend under this rule unless it is satisfied that the person to be appointed satisfies the conditions in rule 21.4(3). ## Appointment of a litigation friend by court order – supplementary

## 21.8

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (1) An application for an order under rule 21.6 or 21.7 must be served on every person on whom, in accordance with rule 6.13 (service on parent, guardian etc.), the claim form must be served. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (2) In the case of a protected party, an application under rule 21.6 must also be served on the protected party, unless the court directs otherwise. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (3) An application for an order under rule 21.7 must also be served on –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (a) the person who is the litigation friend, appearing to act as such, when the application is made; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (b) the proposed litigation friend, if they are not the applicant. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.8] (4) On an application for an order under rule 21.6 or 21.7, the court may appoint the person proposed or any other person who satisfies the conditions  in rule 21.4(3). ## Procedure where appointment of a litigation friend ceases

## 21.9

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (1) When a child who is not a protected party reaches the age of 18, the litigation friend’s appointment ceases. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (2) Where a protected party regains or acquires capacity to conduct the proceedings, the litigation friend’s appointment continues until it is ended by court order. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (3) An application for an order under paragraph (2) may be made by –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (a) the protected party;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (b) the litigation friend; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (c) a party. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (4) The party whose litigation friend’s appointment has ceased must serve notice on the other parties –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (a) stating that the appointment of their litigation friend to act has ceased;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (b) giving the party’s address for service; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (c) stating whether or not they intend to carry on the proceedings. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (5) Where that party was a child, the notice must state that they have reached the age of 18 and be signed by that party personally. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (6) that party does not serve the notice required by paragraph (4) within 28 days after the day on which the appointment ceases the court may, on application, stay or strike out (GL) any claim brought by or defence raised by that party. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.9] (7) The liability of a litigation friend for costs continues until the party concerned serves the notice required under paragraph (4) or the former litigation friend serves notice on the parties that their appointment has ceased. ## Compromise etc. by or on behalf of a child or protected party

## 21.10

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (1) Where a claim is made –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (a) by or on behalf of a child or protected party; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (b) against a child or protected party,

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] no settlement, compromise or payment (including any voluntary interim payment) and no acceptance of money paid into court shall be valid, so far as it relates to the claim by, on behalf of or against the child or protected party, without the approval of the court. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (2) Where –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (a) before proceedings in which a claim is made by or on behalf of, or against, a child or protected party (whether alone or with any other person) are begun, an agreement is reached for a settlement or compromise or a payment (including any voluntary interim payment) which relates to the claim; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (b) the sole purpose of proceedings is to obtain the approval of the court to a settlement or compromise or a payment (including any voluntary interim payment) which relates to the claim,

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] the claim must –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (i) be made using the procedure set out in Part 8 (alternative procedure for claims); and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (ii) include a request to the court for approval of the settlement or compromise or payment (including any voluntary interim payment). [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (3) The documents supporting any application or request for approval must include—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (a) a draft consent order setting out the proposed settlement terms;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (b) details of whether or to what extent liability is admitted;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (c) the age and occupation (if any) of the child or protected party;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (d) confirmation that the litigation friend approves the settlement;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (e) a copy of any relevant medical, financial or other expert evidence or advice;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (f) in a personal injury claim arising from an accident, details of the accident and of claimed loss and damage;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (g) any documents relevant to considerations of liability; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (h) a legal opinion on the merits of the settlement, except in very clear cases, together with any relevant instructions unless they are sufficiently set out in the opinion. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (4) If the claim includes damages for future financial loss, the court must be satisfied that the parties have considered whether the damages should wholly or partly comprise periodical payments. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (5) If the settlement includes periodical payments, the draft consent order must satisfy the requirements of rules 41.8 and 41.9 as appropriate. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (6) In proceedings to which Section IV of Part 45 applies, the court will not make an order for detailed assessment of the costs payable to the child or protected party but will assess the costs in the manner set out in that Section. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (7) Where settlement of a claim by or on behalf of a dependent child includes agreement on a sum to be apportioned to the dependent child, the parties must provide to the court in addition details of—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (a) the claimed loss of future earnings in respect of the deceased;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (b) the nature and extent of the dependency. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.10] (Rule 46.4 contains provisions about costs where money is payable to a child or protected party.)

## Control of money recovered by or on behalf of a child or protected party

## 21.11

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (1) Where in any proceedings –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (a) money is recovered by or on behalf of or for the benefit of a child or protected party; or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (b) money paid into court is accepted by or on behalf of a child or protected party,

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] the money will be dealt with in accordance with directions given by the court under this rule and not otherwise. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (2) Directions given under this rule may provide that the money shall be wholly or partly paid into court and invested or otherwise dealt with. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (3) Where money is recovered by or on behalf of a protected party or money paid into court is accepted by or on behalf of a protected party, before giving directions under this rule, the court will first consider whether the protected party is a protected beneficiary. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (4) Where a child lacks capacity to manage and control any money recovered by or on behalf of the child, and is likely to remain so on reaching full age, the fund will be administered as a protected beneficiary’s fund. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (5) Where a child or protected beneficiary is in receipt of publicly funded legal services the fund shall be subject to a first charge under section 25 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012(1) (statutory charge) and an order for the investment of money on the child’s or protected beneficiary’s behalf must contain a direction to that effect. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (6) The representative or litigation friend of the child or protected beneficiary must apply to the court for directions for management of the fund or payment into court (using Form CFO 320 or CFO 320PB to be completed by the judge), stating the nature and terms of any proposed investment vehicle, with appropriate supporting evidence. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (7) The judge hearing the application may adjourn it and give directions for further information to be provided and, unless the judge directs otherwise, the money recovered will be paid into the court special account pending determination of the application for investment. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (8) Where money is recovered for the benefit of a child who is not a protected beneficiary—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (a) if the court considers it appropriate, it may order that the money be paid directly to the litigation friend to be placed in a bank, building society or similar account for the child’s use;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (b) if the money remains invested in court, it must be paid out to the child when the child reaches the age of 18;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (c) any investments held in court other than money must either be sold and the proceeds paid to the child, or transferred to the child, when the child reaches the age of 18. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (9) Where money is recovered for the benefit of a protected beneficiary—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (a) if the amount is £100,000 or more, subject to (b) below, the court shall direct the litigation friend to apply to the Court of Protection for the appointment of a deputy, after which the fund shall be dealt with as directed by the Court of Protection;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (b) the procedure in sub-paragraph (a) will not apply where a person with authority to administer the protected beneficiary’s financial affairs has been appointed as attorney under a registered enduring power of attorney, or as donee of a registered lasting power of attorney, or as the deputy appointed by the Court of Protection;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (c) any payment out of money must be in accordance with any decision or order of the Court of Protection;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (d) if an application to the Court of Protection is required, that application must be made;

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (e) if the Court of Protection so decides, on its own initiative or at the request of the judge hearing the application for investment, an amount exceeding £100,000 may be retained in court and invested in the same way as the fund of a child. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.11] (10) A request for payment of money from a fund held for the benefit of a child or protected party, or to vary an investment strategy, may be made in writing with appropriate supporting evidence (but without making a formal application) to a Master or District Judge and may be determined without a hearing unless the court directs otherwise. ## Costs and expenses incurred by a litigation friend

## 21.12

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (1) In proceedings to which rule 21.11 applies, a litigation friend who incurs costs or expenses on behalf of a child or protected party in any proceedings is entitled on application to recover the amount paid or payable out of any money recovered or paid into court to the extent that it –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (a) has been reasonably incurred; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (b) is reasonable in amount. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (2) Costs recoverable in respect of a child under this rule are limited to—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (a) costs which have been assessed by way of detailed assessment under rule 46.4(2);

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (b) costs incurred by way of success fee under a conditional fee agreement or sum payable under a damages based agreement in a claim for damages for personal injury where the damages agreed or ordered to be paid do not exceed £25,000, where such costs have been summarily assessed under rule 46.4(5), or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (c) costs incurred where a detailed assessment of costs has been dispensed with under rule 46.4(3) in the circumstances set out in Practice Direction 46. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (3) Expenses may include all or part of –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (a) a premium in respect of a costs insurance policy (as defined by section 58C(5) of the Courts and Legal Services Act 1990); or

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (b) interest on a loan taken out to pay a premium in respect of a costs insurance policy or other recoverable disbursement. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (4) No application may be made under this rule for costs or expenses that –

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (a) are of a type that may be recoverable on an assessment of costs payable by or out of money belonging to a child or protected party; but

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (b) are disallowed in whole or in part on such an assessment. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (Costs and expenses which are also “costs” as defined in rule 44.1(1) are subject to rule 46.4(2) and (3).)

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (5) In deciding whether the costs or expenses were reasonably incurred and reasonable in amount, the court will have regard to all the circumstances of the case including the factors set out in rule 44.4(3) and 46.9. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (6) When the court is considering the factors to be taken into account in assessing the reasonableness of the costs or expenses, it will have regard to the facts and circumstances as they reasonably appeared to the litigation friend or to the child’s or protected party’s legal representative or deputy when the cost or expense was incurred. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (7) Subject to paragraph (7), where the claim is settled or compromised, or judgment is given, on terms that an amount not exceeding £5,000 is paid to the child or protected party, the total amount the litigation friend may recover under paragraph (1) must not exceed 25% of the sum so agreed or awarded, unless the court directs otherwise. Such total amount must not exceed 50% of the sum so agreed or awarded. [PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (8) The amount which the litigation friend may recover under paragraph (1) in respect of costs must not (in proceedings at first instance) exceed 25% of the amount of the sum agreed or awarded in respect of—

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (a) general damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity; and

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (b) damages for past financial loss

[PART 21 – CHILDREN AND PROTECTED PARTIES > 21.12] (9) Except in a case to which Section IV, Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of Part 45 applies, and  where a claim under rule 45.9 or 45.10 has not been made, no application may be made under this rule for a payment out of the money recovered by the child or protected party until the costs payable to the child or protected party have been assessed or agreed.
